resources.string: At most once an hour, when you open WakeNudge. Turn this off and WakeNudge never goes online by itself.
See if a newer version is out

WakeNudge asks GitHub (api.github.com) for the latest release when you open the app, at most once an hour, and when you tap Check now. Nothing about you or your alarms is sent, though GitHub sees your IP address like any website.
Alarms, timers and everything else run on this phone. The only thing that goes online is the optional update check under Updates, which you can switch off.
There is nothing to sign up for and nothing to pay. Your alarms and history stay on this phone, and the update check sends nothing about you.
Camera, activity recognition, NFC and calendar are requested only when you use a feature that needs them. This version also has internet access, used only for the optional update check.
No ads, no accounts, no tracking. The only time WakeNudge goes online is an optional update check (at most once an hour), which you can switch off in About. Everything else stays on your phone.
